title: Electrical Circuits & Instrumentation
description: Circuit analysis, analog electronics, filters, sensors, noise, and data acquisition for physiological and laboratory measurement.

prerequisites.statement: Physics: Electricity & Magnetism; Calculus I recommended

outcomes.description: Solve DC networks with Kirchhoff and Thevenin methods.
Select an amplifier topology for a sensor signal.
Quantify noise, loading, and calibration limits.

lesson_objectives.description: Use nodal analysis for multi-branch networks.
Reduce a source network to Thevenin form.
Apply ideal op-amp assumptions within feedback limits.
Choose an instrumentation architecture for small differential signals.
Compute a first-order RC cutoff frequency.
Explain the Nyquist condition and why it is not enough for real signals.
Model a sensor transfer function and calibration curve.
Propagate uncertainty to a reported measurement.
Analyze a voltage divider and a source with internal resistance using a Thevenin equivalent.
Calculate the loading error when a measuring input of finite resistance is connected, and choose an input resistance that keeps the error below a target.
Compute ADC resolution and convert it into the smallest change in the measured physical quantity, and evaluate which error dominates.
Derive the transfer function of an RC low-pass filter and compute its time constant and cutoff frequency.
Calculate the gain (as a ratio and in decibels) and the phase shift at a given frequency.
Evaluate whether a first-order filter adequately suppresses noise and aliasing for a chosen sampling rate.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

modules.title: DC network analysis and equivalent circuits

lessons.title: DC network analysis and equivalent circuits
lessons.worked_example: A 5 V source with 1 kΩ series resistance driving a 9 kΩ load gives 4.5 V across the load by voltage division.

modules.title: Operational amplifiers and analog front ends

lessons.title: Operational amplifiers and analog front ends
lessons.worked_example: A non-inverting stage with Rf=90 kΩ and Rg=10 kΩ has ideal gain 1+Rf/Rg=10, while actual bandwidth falls as closed-loop gain rises.

lessons.title: Filters, sampling, and anti-aliasing
lessons.worked_example: With R=10 kΩ and C=1 μF, fc≈15.9 Hz; a 100 Hz component is strongly attenuated by a single-pole low-pass stage.

lessons.title: Sensors, calibration, and uncertainty
lessons.worked_example: If V=2x and voltage uncertainty is ±0.02 V, the corresponding first-order x uncertainty is ±0.01 units, assuming slope 2 V/unit and no other error sources.

lessons.title: Reading a sensor without fooling yourself: voltage dividers, loading error and ADC resolution
lessons.worked_example: The divider gives 1.833 V from 3.3 V; a 1 MΩ electrode read by a 10 MΩ input loses 9.1% (and 0.10% at 1 GΩ); a 12-bit ADC on 3.3 V resolves 0.806 mV, or 0.020 °C at 40 mV/°C.

lessons.title: First-order frequency response: an RC low-pass filter for a biological signal
lessons.worked_example: R = 10 kΩ and C = 10 nF give τ = 0.10 ms and f_c = 1591.5 Hz; at 100 Hz the gain is 0.9980 with -3.60° phase, while 10 kHz is attenuated only to 0.157 (-16.1 dB), so a single stage protects poorly against aliasing at 2000 Hz sampling.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added an original lesson on sensor loading and ADC resolution (dividers, Thevenin resistance, input-impedance error, resolution versus accuracy) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added an original lesson on first-order RC low-pass frequency response, decibels, phase and anti-aliasing with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: Four compact legacy units are preserved; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.
There is no authored 12–15 week schedule, substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm, cumulative final, or graded integrative project.

Practice items are short formative checks (two per prototype unit and six per original lesson); they do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery, and objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.

Of the 17 numerical answers in this package, eight require a unit, none checks significant figures and none checks dimensions; the others accept a number within a stated tolerance, with the unit optional.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.
intentionally_omitted: Full instructional sequence and summative assessments are not authored yet; the original lessons extend a partial package.
